own_list: - Lack of remote connectivity to the sensor nodes makes them unlikely to be able to be patched.
- No mention of MQTT transport-layer encryption.
- Pre-shared key if intercepted puts all other nodes within the same fleet at risk.
- No stated key revocation process, ciphers, or other robust PKI controls.
- The telemetry lake has customer data yet it is not clear how it is protected.
- The cloud storage bucket being public read can enable someone to reverse engineer the firmware and find potential vulnerabilities.
- The nodes have no way to verify that the firmware they are installing is legitimate, so a MITM attack might serve up malicious firmware.
- The serial console may not have any authentication, so anyone with local access may be able to modify the firmware -- especially since it is not signed.
